newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom says banks exercise Greenshoe. [CORRECTED 8:26 GMT]
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom says banks exercise Greenshoe. [CORRECTED 8:26 GMT]

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG, the German telecommunications group that was partially privatised last month, said on Tuesday that the banks that managed its listing have fully exercised the so-called "Greenshoe" option.

This option allowed the banks to issue up to 90 million additional shares bringing the total number of shares issued in Europe's largest ever initial public offering to 713.7 million shares, or 26 percent of the company's capital.

Around 67 percent of the issue was placed in Germany, with private investors buying 285 million shares, or 41 percent of the global offering, and institutions buying 177 million shares, or 26 percent.
The company gave the following details on the allocation of shares outside Germany:
United States, Canada, South America 14 98 million
Japan, Asia, Rest of world 5 35 million
The global offering included a basic allotment of 600 million shares, a Greenshoe option of 90 million additional shares, and 23.7 million shares as part of the employee share-holding scheme.
The main underwriters of the global offering were Deutsche Bank, Dresdner Bank and U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs.
